clips.note: the MIRROR of sprintTurnR90: the footage's left and right sprint turns are mirror images (6:04.1-6:04.7 left: the left leg trails while the right plants; 6:00.9-6:01.3 right: the right trails). The right turn's take with flip + a front hint mirrors him exactly (sides swapped, x negated). The left takes tried directly (5:50.30, 6:03.60 back, 5:39.00 side) mirrored, lost a foot or swung the yaw both ways

clips.name: rotateL
clips.title: Rotating in place, left
clips.note: one full turn of the steady spin (front 6:23.12 to front 6:23.82, 0.70 s; the spin speeds up from 0.89 s a turn to about 0.65). The root's yaw is the tool's measured turn scaled to 360; the hips' yaw is keyed every frame (pose_keys, blend 0) so root + hips = the facing read off the footage at each quarter: front 6:23.12, his left side 6:23.30, back 6:23.45, his right side 6:23.65, front 6:23.82. ground body (no foot is found planted in the spin: without it the hips floated 0.25 m), travel 0 (he circles on the spot)

clips.name: rotateR
clips.title: Rotating in place, right
clips.note: the MIRROR of rotateL (its take with flip and a back hint, its hips keys negated): the right spin's own takes (6:26.43, 6:27.10: front to front, 0.69 s a turn, the same speed) start with the tracker reading the front view as a back view, which twists his chest 180 degrees against his hips
